en: The *Lokeśvaraśataka*, composed by Ācārya Vajradatta. Om, homage to Lokeśvara!
On the head of the Lord of Heaven, who wears a crown and bows down, they possess the luster of radiant rubies;
on the head of the Lotus-Seated One, who is bowed in devotion, they resemble a smiling garland of *mālatī* flowers;
and on the head of Śambhu, as the moon wanes, they diminish its thick, tawny hue.
May the moon-like splendors of the stainless toenails of Lokeśvara’s feet bring peace to the world. || 1 ||
It was not indeed shaken off by the powerful rays of the moon on Śiva’s matted locks, which were variegated by their contact with the tawny hair;
nor was it removed by the intense splendor of the rubies in Viṣṇu’s crown;
nor did it dissolve into the mass of dark, curling locks of the gods as they sported.
May the irresistible splendors of the toenails of the Goddesses of the World be for the quelling of your darkness. || 2 ||
He is the cause for the attainment of the full expansion of lotuses within the vast treasury of his belly;
he removes the fear of the calamities of the wicked from people whose beloved ones have departed;
and even by those who leap up with insults, he has quelled the terror arising from the malignant seizure of darkness.
May that unprecedented moonlight of the cool luster of the toenails on the feet of Lokeśa purify you. || 3 ||
May your lofty crests of flame— the great fire that utterly consumes the fuel of the mass of afflictions—
dispel the dense darkness of delusion bound within the three worlds by their playful light;
may they be unfailing showers of the waters of nectar upon the masses of fire in the realms of hell.
The splendors of the multitude of his toenails, born from the feet of the Lotus-Bearer, destroy the cycle of worldly existence.
Of those inconceivable wish-fulfilling gems (*cintāmaṇi*), which are skillful in granting desires that cut through self-will;
which are enchanting in their ability to quell the arising of intense dread and apprehension;
and which possess the luster of a mirror-image sustained by a multitude of various qualities clearly manifested, [there is] the radiance of necklaces.
May the shadow of the toenails of the Lord of the World, which shine forth from his feet, protect you. || 5 ||
May that mass of the luster of the Lord’s toenails— which shines with the brilliance of His lofty, upward-pointing crown, and which is radiant with the splendor of His high crest— long protect you;
for it rises even higher than the heap of beautiful jewels upon the heads of the gods who are expert in worshipping Him.
The service of Śacī was performed with a bow as bright as a mass of light rays emanating in various ways.
Bestowing the attainment of desired objects upon those who serve them— beings who are never deficient in their rise toward glorious enjoyments—
they generate joy with an unswerving luster on all sides; and by virtue of their stainlessness, they mock the moon with their incomparable reflections, having severed the defects of darkness.
May the toenails of the lotus-handed one grant you praise, like ruby lamps at his two feet. 7.
May that sprout of the lotuses of the feet of the King of Kings— produced by the luster of his multitude of toenails— be the destroyer of the heavy burden of your intense fears of worldly existence;
for it has arisen from the soil of his body, having bestowed its aid through a cloud of incessant compassion.
He who is no small man, having taken up the seeds of wisdom like a multitude of sprouts from the wish-fulfilling tree.
The rays from the toenails of Lokeśvara’s lotus-feet, which dispel the terror of the army of Śiva,
possess the splendor of unerring arrows with tips directed toward his crimson quiver;
they serve as ever-ready ropes for lifting up those people fallen into the dreadful pit of saṃsāra.
May these ascending shoots cause you to ascend to the lofty state of great prosperity, which is otherwise difficult to attain.
Radiant, heroes in severing the heat of the world rendered helpless by the toil of afflictions and karma,

teachers of keen intellect who perceive faults from afar, bestowing intense bliss upon people, and possessing the splendor of the full moon— may those stainless stars [of the Buddhas] grant protection.
May those whose lotus-hand nails dispel the inconceivable thoughts of Māra be victorious! 10.
Is this an offering fashioned from fragments of the radiant crescent moon by Śambhu?
Or is it a necklace of jewels placed here by the Goddess of Enlightenment out of unsurpassed longing?
Or perhaps it is a garland of divine and wondrous, peerless flowers suspended by the gods?
May the thought, "May the row of the Lord of the World’s toenails be pleasing," which is born from His feet, arise within you. 11.

Where is this lotus-born one, whose foot-dust has long rested upon the bed of the lofty rubies on the heads of bowing gods; and where is this prostration with the crown of the head touching the surface of the earth?
Thus, as if bursting into laughter through their massed rays, those [beams] which are jagged and difficult to endure—
May those nails of the Lord of the World, born from his feet, be for the destruction of darkness in you. 12.
They are heroes in the removal of heat, creating showers of the most cooling nectar-drops; they are ramparts against the destruction caused by the cruel and far-reaching torrent of fierce arrows;
[they are the remedy for] the various kinds of noble suffering within the vast belly of the prison-house that is the form of saṃsāra.
May the splendors of the toenails of the glorious lotus-handed Lord, which bring prosperity, destroy your terrible [suffering].

The splendors arising from the toenails of the feet of Lokeśa produce the illusion of a curtain-like screen that obstructs the all-pervading arrows released by Māra, who is difficult to resist from afar;
they are like a mass of great banners clearly proclaiming the destruction of the army of afflictions.
Victorious are those great Vaijayantī banners of victory over the three worlds, possessing powers impossible for the three realms of existence to overcome. || 14 ||

The mind of perfect enlightenment shines like the mass of light from the moon; it is like a great heap of ashes from the burnt-out fires of the afflictions, scattered by the wind of the path to liberation;
and it is as indestructible as a slab of flawless, pure white stone set down by the cruel Māras.
May the mass of luster from the toe-nails of the lotus-handed one, imagined as a peacock, protect you. || 15 ||

Those who for a moment must be gazed upon with embarrassment by the Lord of Nights (the Moon)— who is himself incapable of dispelling the peerless darkness of the nights due to his own calamity consisting of the unimpaired waning of his phases; yet who possess stainless and imperishable eyes,
and whose initiation in protecting the world is unimpaired and skilled in destroying the faction of enemies that has not been diminished.
May those toe-nails of Lokeśvara protect you from the onset of misfortune in this world. (16)

May the incomparable height of the mass of light from the nails of the Lord— who possesses the six perfections as his means, who takes refuge in the fortress of the feet of the excellent lotus-bearer (Viṣṇu), and who desires to conquer the glory of the three worlds— bring you prosperity;
for that mass has clearly attained extreme growth by circling around its friend, the sun, which has reached its full rising.
May she—who is the cause for the great success of the Mahāyāna against the enemies of all calamities and misfortunes—protect us! || 17 ||
Shameless, Paśupati bears his desire for the crescent-moon ornament upon his crest;

the longing for splendor in Śauri’s Kaustubha gem somehow subsides in the presence of the fortunate [Śiva]. Yet, when he is seen, even that [Kaustubha] becomes useless, for [Śiva] possesses a great crown set with Indra’s jewels—thus [it is said] by those of discerning minds.
May that multitude of toe-nails of the Lotus-handed One be victorious, which was not even conceived of by the worlds because of its splendor. || 18 ||
Rising high and far-reaching above, yet spreading its canopy below for the denizens of hell;
possessing the luster of rising frost, pure, and the cause of the destruction of the darkness in the faces of enemies;
its power difficult to comprehend, it is the light that makes the entire world clearly visible.
May the mass of rays from the nails of the lotus-feet resting upon the crown of the Buddha protect you. || 19 ||
Behold the mountain, radiant with the camphor powder released by the clever young wives of the joyful Lord of the Immortals as they worship him;
its ground shimmering with the ashes from the matted locks of Śiva, who is inclined by the weight of his devotion;
and where the fine pollen from the tips of the filaments falls from the lotus-hands of Lakṣmī, scattered during her ritual offerings.
May the multitude of rays from the nails of the hand and foot born of the one who holds a lotus protect you from the lower realms. || 20 ||

The mass of light from my claws, which has drunk up the yellow luster [of the sun], which possesses a crimson beauty like the thick powder of vermilion from the temples of the gods' elephants, which has pacified the hero Śūra (the Sun) by robbing him of his green horse’s speed,
and which bears a dark-blue hue as it closes upon the lotus-foot of the Lotus-Bearer (Viṣṇu)— [may that mass of light protect you].
May He protect you—He who was gazed upon by the wives of the gods, trembling with fear at the swelling of the rising ocean of milk. || 21 ||
"O Rambhā, beauty is already conceived in this [palanquin] by means of fly-whisks as white as the moon;

why do you vainly scatter camphor powder with such devoted effort? What need have you for these scattered flowers, pure as Śacī?"—thus was it said to you, the celestial nymphs, by your lord, the Lord of the Heavens.
May the mass of light from the toenails of the Lotus-Handed One, described during his worship, protect you.

On Mount Vindhya, which outshines Kailāsa, wherein the blackness of the body of the Conqueror of Bali (Kṛṣṇa) has been swallowed up, which is anointed with the playful beauty of Kālī, and where the rays of the sun have lost their greenish-yellow hue;
[there] the mass of rays from the great nails of the Lord of the World (Viṣṇu) has, as it were, shattered itself, thinking, "What am I compared to this?"
May the moon protect you under the guise of the sacrificial pit, which is crowded with gods and demons skilled in worship. || 23 ||
The feet of the Buddha’s crown-nails, which bear an immense expanse of rays arising from their soles,
act as a great bridge for crossing the ocean of saṃsāra;
they are a mass of water consisting of the great accumulation of merit that extinguishes the rising fire of insurmountable suffering.
May [those things] which, possessing the brilliance of a flash of lightning, suddenly effect the shattering of your worldly existence, [protect you]. 24.
It is a humiliation of the moon’s splendor beloved by Kālī; it is a mockery of the laughter of the light of the vast Mount Kailāsa; it is a destruction of the dignity of the Himalayan whiteness;
and even the flooding of the quarters with the waters of the Ocean of Milk is [no match for] the tusks of the celestial elephant.
May the spreading luster of the nails on the feet of the Lord of the World protect you—luster that is like a shadow of destruction to [the pride of] those who have been wounded. || 25 ||
Where the bee-swarm that had gathered upon the *Pūjāpārijāta* tree closed its eyes as it settled on the lotus of Śrī;
where the Self-born One (Brahmā), intent on service, remained perched upon a budding lotus;
and by whom the day’s splendor was turned dark, while the night—having quelled the fatigue of the celestial damsels—was brought forth.
May that foot of Padmapāṇi, with the moonlight shimmering from its crescent-like nails, protect you all. || 26 ||
The beloved one, honored by the glances of the women of the gods whose husbands were distraught,
bore a brilliant splendor arising from the luster of his nails like a cluster of white lotus stalks;
he was like a lover who, overcome by the expansion of manifold desires, has set out upon a solitary journey.
May your foot, which is joyfully anointed with the sandalwood from the city of the gods, protect you—[the foot] of Padmapāṇi. || 27 ||

May Śrī bestow abundant welfare upon you— she who emerged from the midst of the milk-ocean, which was filled with the rays of her stainless nails like a mass of shimmering lightning, while the celestial beings scattered Pārijāta flowers with hands radiant with the luster of bliss, resembling a swarm of buzzing bees over the thick expanse of Kālīya’s deadly Kālakūṭa poison.
Rising from the lotus-foot of Padmapāṇi, which is the cause of Acyuta’s delight. || 28 ||

May [the Lord’s hand], which possesses a great abundance of splendor—splendor that conceals the bees shimmering like the reflection of a lotus; which cuts through the flames of the fire surging from the exhaustion of frustrated desires;
and which is rendered magnificent by clusters of pure nail-rays swelling with their own unobstructed and overflowing luster—protect you.
May his foot, with rays from its hand-like fingers tinted by the luster of a lotus, grant our desires effortlessly and without interruption. 29.
Possessing the splendor of the arisen and radiant wheel, with the luster of stainless nails, his glory has risen without peer;
bearing the multitude of marks brought about by incomparable virtues and incalculable merit, he is the great majesty arising from the lamp of all continents— the Buddha, the crown jewel.
May that foot of the Lord of the World, which is the sovereign over the circle of heads of those who bow down, protect you for a long time. || 30 ||

"What merit is there in this [moon] with its scattered buds of the golden lotuses of the celestial Ganges? What is the use of songs sung by swarms of bees, who mistake them for clearly visible lotuses?
"No," she replied, "it is possible for strings of rubies to shine upon these lustrous nails."
Victorious is that foot of the Lord of Gods, which is worshipped by one whose hands are busy with lotuses.
He who was indeed not even a cause for the birth of the Protector, the Sugata, for those living beings;
he upon whom neither a swarm of bees nor even a person with partiality felt a longing for a lotus;
by him, though exceedingly humble, the three worlds were made to bow before the Earth, which was itself no longer too heavy.
May that foot protect the world—the foot of him whose crown is illuminated by the radiance of the moon-like Sugata.

May that Lord of the World, whose mass of dust rests upon the heads of the immortals, grant you long-lasting prosperity— he who, by bestowing drink upon the weary, brought joy to his assembly of servants; he in whom there was no lack of excellence, for he was indeed the very foundation for the ultimate beauty of the greenery.
The lotus-foot is the ground for the abode of prosperity and the highest good, its filaments laughing with the rays of light from the nails.

The weapon brought about by the violent impulse of those who inflict harm upon the body is an invocation for the failure of their worldly efforts; it is the destruction of the great majesty of the vast ones,
and it is the burning of the fire of suffering caused by the great hostility toward those who have performed oblations to dispel the host of afflictions.
May she who holds a lotus in her hand and whose feet are the source of existence be a river that carries away [suffering] and bestows manifold benefits. || 34 ||

May the swarm of bees, bearing the illusion of a complete lotus upon the crown-jewel that is the Buddha’s ornament, eloquent yet free from discursive thought, bestow prosperity upon you as it glides toward his feet—
for the sake of establishing the firm, most enduring, and long-lasting state of those whose sole task is the protection of sentient beings.
It was fastened like a chain of thick black iron by her abundant compassion.
With petals as beautiful as the inner leaves of a lotus, soft yet possessing the essence of a diamond,
it is the ground for the shattering of the multitude of weapons hurled by enraged enemies;
red, it is the cause of the supreme power that brings about the pacification of passion and leads to liberation.
May the foot of the Sugata, who bears the moon, be for you the remover of fatigue from the ocean of saṃsāra. || 36 ||
The restless bee, though fickle, does not cling even out of caprice to the cluster of lotuses blooming from the mouth of Jambhāri;
nor does it settle upon the heap of *kunda* flowers that bring joy to Śiva;
nor does it alight upon the radiant, fragrant *pārijāta* tree strewn by Viṣṇu before him—[yet it remains unattached].
May that lotus-foot of the Victor, wherein the swarm of bees delights with joy, protect you. || 37 ||
May he who is radiant with a mane shining from a mass of intensely risen luster; who is formidable with the splendor of his upward-pointing claws and fangs, suffused with a crimson glow;
and who is to be gazed upon by the trembling, flickering eyes of the fleeing enemies who are like elephants—may he be for your prosperity.
May the lion at the feet of Lokeśa, who reclines in the forest of Brahmā’s matted locks, lead you to auspiciousness. 38.
Though clear, it was not clear; though light, it was not light to traverse the quarters of the sky;

though a source of joy to the three worlds, it was the cause of intense, pervasive torment for others’ bodies; though smeared with the ointment of loveliness, it was exceedingly sweet yet the suppressor of the pain of misfortune.
May the radiance from the foot of the one whose crest is a garland of blossoming lotuses (jinaruci) bring you illumination. 39.
The King of Kings rejoiced with *rājīva* lotuses; Hari also with green and captivating *pārijāta* trees; the Moon with *kunda* blossoms; Indra with radiant showers of abundant wealth;
and Varuṇa was pleased with *palāśa* flowers—thus the host of gods offered this distinguished and profuse worship.
May that foot of the lotus-handed one, which has been treated as poetry through alliteration, protect you. (40)

The Sun, looking up at his nails, offered praise during their radiance; the Lord of Heaven (Indra) did so at the tips of his claws; Śiva at the joints of his fingers; and even Antaka (Yama), with unblinking eyes, at the beauty of their extremities—for he was unable to perceive the extraordinary excellence that lay beyond the scope of ordinary splendor.
Victorious is that foot of the one whose crown is marked by the image of the Buddha, which completely surpasses the divine worlds. 41.

May the foot of the mountain that bears the lotus— the form of which is as majestic as a thicket of thick, matted locks radiant with the sun of the Perfectly Awakened One, and which acts as a pillar for the earth of the masses of people sinking in the ocean of saṃsāra— be for your welfare, as it is served by the caravans of the Siddhas.
May he, from whose extremities flows a great stream of red mineral-essence dripping with radiant luster, protect you. || 42 ||

May the tree of the feet of the Lord of the World grant you prosperity—its shade being the cause for the complete pacification of the exhaustion and weariness of all beings on the long journey of saṃsāra; its branches resplendent with the flowers of its manifest nails;
and its basin the garlands of crowns offered by the gods who bow before it.
May the sprinkling of pure light-water from the jar-like crest-jewel, accomplished at the root, protect you. 43.

May his foot protect you—the foot that bears incomparable, stainless lotuses; which has attained the joy of uprooting the powerful enemy force of the dense web of fundamental afflictions (kleśa); which is the abode of the playful sport of the crowns of victorious heroes; and which, through its deceptive blossoming, causes the longing for [ordinary] blooming lotuses to fade.
He is one whose longing for music is eclipsed by the swarms of bees, thick with restless and abundant humming, as they hover about.
May he be the tethering-post for the restless female elephant of the fortune of sovereignty over the three worlds;
the bear (Rāhu) skilled in protecting the entire world when it falters from the bite of the serpent of painful affliction;
and the firm bolt on the gate of the city of hell, which is otherwise difficult to enter and never thins out—may he protect you all.
May the foot of the Lord of the World be for prosperity—the sole raft for crossing the ocean of worldly existence. || 45 ||
Thus ended the instruction on the foot-stool; the manner of dancing ceased, and the faultless science of instrumental music was suddenly dissolved;
neither song nor its censure was heard, nor were the aesthetic emotions brought forth by those who had fashioned the compositions of rasa.

Victorious is that Lotus-born One, whose form produces insatiable longing, in whose assembly Indra’s court—though filled with celestial nymphs eager for love—was unable to perform worship, even as they smiled from within. 46.
He who crushes Māra and pride through the fierce, unrestrained, and leftward (vāma) sequence of his power;
whose crown possesses immeasurable great splendor arising from the destruction of delusion at its center; who is terrifying in his vastness;
the glorious one whose abode is the great desire for a majesty equal to boundless existence in the state of supreme abundance.
May he, whose gentle mind is renowned for its boundless love for all beings, and who is the refuge of the tireless, be for your protection. || 47 ||

To him who, for those terrified by the causes of suffering, provides the refuge of remembrance within the belly of the prison— a place where the formidable enclosures of solid walls act as obstructions, and which possesses the fierce, vast, and terrifying appearance of the city-dweller of hell— [to that Lord, I bow].
May Lokeśvara, who acts with hospitality and possesses profound compassion, protect you as he has come. || 48 ||
Leaping amidst the ocean— whose waters are turbid and crowded with swarms of crocodiles, made resonant by rows of tossing waves stirred by the playful winds blowing at the end of an aeon—
he took his stand, possessing the grace of one reclining upon the vast, pure, blue-lotus-studded pavement of the earth.
May that most gentle one, who is the lotus-born Brahmā, be capable of protecting him in this world. 49.

The mass of smoke from whose name— when it is held by those who maintain the continuity of its study— becomes even a fire that binds the distressed moon with its bonds, obstructs the persistent radiance of the sun, and is preeminent in uprooting the fortitude of the wives of the gods who are bewildered by the affliction of blocked passages.
May that Dhāraṇī of the Buddha, which brings about the complete destruction of the cycle of existence, grant you boundless and perfect steadfastness.
With his mass of hands raised in anger holding iron weapons, emitting cruel hissing sounds, his vast body suddenly darkened by swarms of bees clustering on his temples moist with the flow of rut,
the lordly elephant— miserable from the stroke of the goad named [the King’s] Name— was overcome by that wretched man.
May that Lord of the World, whose compassion provides all desired requisites, perform for you the work of fulfilling every wish. || 51 ||
The venomous serpents— the fire of whose wrath was fueled by the heat of their hissing breaths and the emaciation caused by poison— and who displayed their fangs with heads repeatedly raised,

perished when their poison entered the minds of those who were enemies of the Lord of Serpents (Śiva); thus, the powerless are destroyed when they encounter one who hates the sovereign of venomous snakes.
May that Lord of the World be for the pacification of the mass of most difficult afflictions of all beings. 52.

The lion, whose fierce speed was like a song for devouring herds of elephants seized by the heavy pride of belching forth ichor, who moved with impetuous force and roared with deep resonance from the caverns of his thick neck,
attained the state of being yoked to vehicles through the power of the hymns sung by his retinue.
May that yogi, whose lofty and noble head is unattached to the Sugata, ward off your misfortune. || 53 ||
Furthermore, that host— whose hearts were wounded by grief, who caused terror,

who was once steadfast and comparable to mountains, whose bodies possessed the luster of bees, cows, and deer— having abandoned [the field], vanished instantly as if composed of illusion through a stratagem of the gods; its valor departed, it was to be inferred only from its past misfortunes.
May that abode of the Sugatas, which is the son of her whose feet are meditated upon, arise for your victory. || 54 ||

The river of the enemy’s army—whose waters are the essence of their fierce battle against him who serves [the Lord] as a virtuous boatman; whose terrifying dwelling-place is the Kali age, abounding in crocodiles and monsters; whose turbulent waves are the flashing lances and swords; and whose foam and laughter are the outspread, white, shimmering banners—[is crossed by him].
May that lotus-born one, who moves about with enthusiasm through pleasure and pain, gather all happiness for you.
The thunderbolt, possessing the sovereign power to shatter the multitude of mountains, bearing a brilliance as formidable as the vast enjoyment of the earth,
and appearing like the fire at the end of an aeon due to the agitation and confusion caused by the excessive weight of existence,
fell swiftly upon the ground of the navel of those who were struck with fear.
By the power of whose devotion may he be the destroyer of worldly existence, radiant like a lotus held in his hand. || 56 ||

His fortitude shaken by afflictions, standing on the verge of death, pierced by the cruel arrows of anger, his body oppressed by many various diseases difficult to endure due to the obstruction of pain—
he whose mind was sustained by the application of meditation, which infused the nectar of supreme steadfastness— [was liberated].
May he, the possessor of supernatural powers, who is not subject to suffering, whose head is the Buddha, protect your intellect for the sake of awakening.

The lord of the earth, whose fame for the suppression of enemies resounds far and wide through his incomparable majesty, who by his administration of justice has surpassed the renown of Yama, the Lord of the Dead, and who is himself the personification of *daṇḍanīti*—
even the spirits, whose minds were once enraged, now attain great delight through the power of the knowledge of his feet.
May that abode of the bull-like Jina, which is the cause for the arising of contradictions [in opposing views], take away your fear. 58.

Brahmā was rendered speechless, even Agni became a teacher [of silence], Viṣṇu— whose words to Indra had been broken— remained silent and diffident in composing speech, and Śiva, though free from pride, was humbled;
thus it is clear that while the gods were satisfied, they were not truly wise when it came to praising his virtues.
Victorious is that glorious one, the lotus-holder, whose multitude of virtues lies within the range of the Victor’s mind. || 59 ||

The Creator performed a wondrous feat: with his three eyes he became the enemy of the enemies of the gods; with his lineage he became the enemy of the mountains; with his great body he became the refuge for the night-stalkers (the moon);
and with his son, who loves all the world as his own children, he became a friend to his friends.
May that Lord with the lotus in his hand, who is beyond all measure, protect you—he by whom this vessel of praise has been extolled.
In whom Brahmā found manifoldness through his many mouths, Skanda joy-filled abundance in his hymns and prostrations, and even the Lord of Serpents the multitude of his own heads;
and Śakra, beholding him, brought forth the praiseworthy power of his thousand eyes throughout the three worlds— him [I worship].
May that Lord of the World, the worthy recipient of hymns from those whose eyes delight in uninterrupted devotion, protect us. 61.
The sun, whose rays are intensely blazing, indeed remains fruitlessly upon his path;

yet the heat of the lotus-bearing one’s majesty endures for the sake of illuminating the world. Thus was praise offered by the steadfast ones to those assemblies of light, which had manifested with radiant splendor.
Therefore, may that noble one’s favor, which swiftly bestows grace upon his enemies in this world, be granted to me. 62.
In whom, who possesses peerless and singular honor as the abode of merit, even the act of bowing down is itself the highest exaltation for those devoted to him; in whom,
the object of meditation, even the mere remembrance instantly causes the forgetting of all fear of worldly existence.
May that Lord of the World, who has established the path of welfare in the infinite and inconceivable world, protect you. || 63 ||

The thunderbolt of Indra, the destroyer of the enemies of the gods, was rendered useless in some places; that captivating [weapon], though exceedingly sharp, became fruitless against the rows of arrows of the powerful king.
"Hari (Viṣṇu) achieved no purpose with his discus," thus the people surely cried out, "Alas! Alas!"—the sound of their lamentation.
Victory to the lotus-faced one, who delights the enemies of Cupid and who is free from attachment to worldly expansion.

He who maintains a bliss transcending the world yet suffers with the intense suffering of the worlds; who is eternally compassionate toward helpless and wretched living beings though he is himself eternally free from attachment; and who, though the sole lord of the three realms, is devoted to pleasing the people through his incomparable beauty.
May he, whose crown is the Fully Awakened One and who has performed inconceivable deeds unlike any other, protect you for a long time. || 65 ||
May that Lamp of the Lord of the World be victorious, whose application to the peerless love established throughout the three worlds is uninterrupted;
who, being extinguished, cannot be shaken by the powerful and heavy winds of the mad heretics;
and who dispels the darkness of delusion arisen within the mansion of the universe.
He is the destruction [of suffering], whose abode is indestructible, and whose course is established through the exertion of performing what is beneficial for others.
Where is this universal loving-kindness, and where is the burning hatred toward the thick and uneven afflictions?

Where is the mature power of liberation, and where is the firm binding by the noose of compassion? Where is the partiality of indifference, and where is the preoccupation with acting for the benefit of others? Such is its wondrous variety!
Wondrous is the deed of the Lotus-handed One; may it become for you a light that conquers even the world beyond. 67.
Foremost of all, possessing a vast method for the manifestation of every form, always the protector of all,
he exists in every way for the sake of accomplishing the great and universal purpose of the discipline of all;
by means of all his teacherly qualities of majesty and excellence, which crush the pride of all, he humbles every arrogance.
May He, the giver of everything to all, the crown of all omniscient ones, fulfill your vast desires.

"The Lord, the Master, the Protector of Creatures, the Preceptor of the Immortals, the Guardian of the World, the Great Indra, the Radiant One, the Bestower of Punishment upon Enemies, the Conqueror of the Strength of Foes, the Giver of Wealth, the Conquering Noose"—
while his own attendants were thus speaking with names that accorded to their true nature, their speech was filled with suppressed laughter.
May that Lord with the lotus in his hand be victorious, before whose alms-bowl the hosts of gods bowed down out of modesty.

May that Saṃvara protect you—he who is the most excellent among the best of the noble; who dispels the distress of those seeking supreme boons; who bears immeasurable rays of light; who is difficult for the hosts of enemy heroes to restrain;
who is a hero who subdues heroic foes; and who possesses a vast, noble, and abundant flood of water.
May he be like a cloud, unsteady in its bearing as it pours forth a vast, wide-spreading, and copious downpour of rain.

Having considered that the entire world of beings, led by Nāthī, was like a traveler on the path of the ocean of saṃsāra, he— ever-diligent, exceedingly powerful, and possessing a hand radiant as a lotus—
placed his burden upon him who was capable, and being of great compassion, he attained the state of the Lamp of the Universe.
May that Buddha—who has made his vow fruitful and who maintains the support of steadfastness—protect you with his peace. || 71 ||
Exalted and most venerable like the Sugata, he bore upon his hand the heavy burden of the world’s manifold duties, as if it were the auspicious Goddess Lakṣmī herself;
and he brought the multitude of sentient beings to the long-desired extinction of the fires of hell.
May he by whom the continuous flow of intense afflictions was stilled, as if [stopping] people, protect you. 72.
He who, though renowned for the power to manifest various infinite forms, is free from illusion;
who, though all fears have been stilled within him, acts with timidity out of extreme compassion;
and who, though devoid of anger, is constantly bound by the "wrath" of the Buddhas for the sake of subduing those with evil intentions.
Victorious is he, whose crown shines with the Fully Awakened One; though the object of contemplation for the great, he is himself inconceivable. || 73 ||
He does not bear a head, but rather a body as beautiful as the light of Amitābha;

he possesses no lotus as an ornament, yet even the enemy host, distressed by great fear, bows before him; though occupied with destroying the world's enemies, he has not bound his matted locks into a topknot.
May that skillful Lord of the World protect you from the sight of the face of an enraged Yama. || 74 ||
The ocean of existence trembled, fearing for its remnants; the multitude of afflictions perished;
and even the Sage, resting in his state, shone with the praiseworthy play of nirvāṇa.
When he, having girded his loins, set forth to perform the work of benefiting all sentient beings on every side—
May he, the crown jewel of the abodes of the Sugatas, thoroughly cleanse the impurities from you through his exertion. 75.
Thus ends the description of the Blessed One.

For the sake of destroying the world’s enemies, Padmapāṇi [descended] upon a ground difficult even for the mind to conceive— a ground where the obstruction of the array of impediments was shattered and where even ritual action brought about absolute peace.

May that exceedingly weighty power of the Lord— by which one who is subservient, bought, or terrified acts as if by a stronger force, and by which one appointed remains free from agitation— protect you from the merciless Destroyer.
The ground of the Tathāgata is indeed not subject to being surpassed, for even though it is most gentle, it simultaneously and intensely illuminates infinite world-systems to pacify all fear;
its splendor eclipses the entire brilliance of all luminous beings, rendering them like the mere flicker of a firefly’s glow.
May Tejā Lokeśvara remove from your hearts the thick darkness of worldly delusion. || 77 ||
Like a person who has fulfilled all hopes, the entire expanse of space was filled on every side;
like the disappearance of all lights, the destruction of the mass of unsurpassed misfortunes began.
Together with the dense darknesses, the great Māra, possessed of vast supernatural power, met his end.
May that splendor of the one who bears the lotus arise for your prosperity; may it be born for you. || 78 ||

He is the Lord who destroys the manifestation of other [gods], the shatterer of Bala, the incomparable sun of heat to the mass of darkness that is difficult to subdue, the scorcher of those whose intentions are hostile toward living beings,
the infallible one who is a wondrous light, and the wielder of power to illuminate objects obstructed by various infinite mountains and the like.
May that single manifestation of Lokeśa, who resembles a host of immortals, be for your destruction of fear. || 79 ||

In this [ocean of existence], where there is the pleasure of the desires of abundant aquatic creatures consisting of all perfected beings, and where the caravans of heterodox teachers— who are a source of harm to people— sink downwards like mountains into that which is distant and difficult to cross;
there spreads on all sides this irresistible [flood] that expands from the intense agitation for the non-existence of the vast world of cyclic existence.
May that ocean of the splendor of his lotus-like hand expand for you, in order to extinguish the fire of fear.
If the fire of hell is actually Nirvāṇa; if the flood of the nectar of Dharma is bound in a mass of matted locks for those to be converted; if the enemy of Death is motionless;
and if the Jina dwells as a venerable kinsman within the house of the head—then what is this threefold world?
May this manifold conduct of the Lord, the Friend of the World, which is free from worldly attachment, destroy your [sins]. 81.
Though singular, she expands through the delightful diversity of forms fashioned by the power of the disposition of sentient beings;
she is a thunderbolt-point of immense, shifting, and unshakable onset, difficult to pierce and consisting of unreal conceptualization.
She is the consort of Lokanātha, the moonlight for the night-lotuses of noble wisdom, and the destroyer of the millions of misfortunes of the non-Buddhist teachers.
May this teaching, which is like the sun that causes the darkness to vanish, be for the destruction of worldly existence and for your instruction. || 82 ||

The dispute, which was a locus for various rising controversies among proponents such as Kaṇāda and Akṣapāda— abounding in intoxicants like *durvāda* (false speech) and *unmādana* (delusion)— was a contentious debate involving both the existent and the non-existent; yet it was the destruction of the calamities of intoxicated people accompanied by pride, and the grace of the learned.
Victorious is the doctrine of the non-arising of phenomena, which crowns the feet of the one who possesses the body of a Jina.

May that hand of the Lotus-handed One stand as a refuge— his hand which has cast away the weapons of his enemies, whose mass of rays shines throughout the three worlds, praised by the gods, possessing vast waters, and whose spreading light destroys the heat of those dwelling in the abode of the Maruts; and may he, who wields the thunderbolt against Bala and Bali, be victorious.
"O You who are praised for the destruction of the fear that expands throughout the entire three worlds, [I bow] to You who are free from destruction. || 84 ||
Capable of uprooting the rows of lofty mountains and trees in the regions where the winds of cosmic dissolution swirl and surge, he has severed the great pride of his enemies' elephants;
he is the noble elephant of the Lord of the World, raining down a flood of ichor that attracts the bees of his devotees.
May you, who are like elephants with trunks in hand, be sufficient for the destruction of the city of the enemy of worldly existence. || 85 ||
Possessing six treasuries as its storehouse, it has attained a state resembling the hundred-edged sword for the sake of fulfilling the desired attainment of the Victor’s splendor;
it is never abandoned by the very praise of the virtues that serve as the dwelling place for the glory of perfect enlightenment.
May the lotus-hand of the Lord of the World be sufficient for you as the cause of liberation. || 86 ||
That true lotus which dwells within the glory of enlightenment, which produces joy for the multitude of ghosts distressed in their mountain caves by throats parched with ever-increasing thirst,
and which is the station of service for the virtuous whose minds are fixed on the desire for prosperity— that is the true lotus.
May that [lotus] of the Lord of the World, possessing a row of rows of brilliant clusters of rays, protect you. 87.

May that [Buddha], who causes people to resemble a parasol— protecting them from the sun of afflictions that intensely heats the dense mass of the spreading rays of manifold sufferings and makes their faces withered and dejected—
never come to grief, for he is the canopy of the sun that is not inferior to any in all the worlds.
May that stainless lotus, resting in the hand of Lokeśa, lead away your mental dejection. || 88 ||
It is the station of power, the great locus of majesty, the abode of splendors, the home of vastness;
it is the dwelling of enemies, the ground for the arising of the destruction of fear born from an existence difficult to overcome,
and the lovely, beautiful, and tranquil residence of the mass that expands with world-surpassing valor.
May the arm of Lokeśa be victorious, a fierce staff for the destruction of the harm inflicted upon many worlds. 89.
Though it pours forth a flood of the nectar of loveliness that causes only distress to enemies, it grants no satisfaction to their eyes; rather, it bestows immense pleasure upon their own.
It is the abode of beauty that eclipses all the ornaments of the entire world, yet it is itself the ornament of ornaments.
May that single lock of hair, which dispels both pleasure and pain, shine for you like the sun over a lotus.

In this ocean of loveliness, the eyes of the meritorious—which had grown withered through pride in their own beauty—attained fruitfulness; yet they met their destruction there by those eyes trembling excessively with craving.
I believe that countless incomparable and radiant beings, such as the moon and others, must have been created [by it].
If even one face of his were victorious, it would surpass the lotus-face of the Lotus-handed One. || 91 ||

In that [place], for those who harbor enmity, there occurred repeatedly a most manifest and burning foul weather— a torrential downpour of the mass of waters from clouds of incessantly shimmering splendor;
yet, the continuous smears of thick, dark ink-paste, along with their persistent attachments, were washed away and destroyed.
May that temple, facing upward, bestowing supreme bliss, and performing various activities, protect you. 92.
Of him whose hands are unwearied by the performance of sacrifices, who sits upon the edge of a clearly defined and vast jeweled floor within his palace,
whose splendor possesses a power of radiance as bright as the massed brilliance of Amitābha,
and whose dense upper construction is unseen because he is pervaded by beauty— [of him] there is a binding of fierce majesty.
May the armor of the immutable Lord, which is the friend of the pungent matted locks, protect you from the distress of the wicked.

Sprinkled by the waters of the mass of Amitābha’s radiance— an incessant and vast flow that is the cause of ultimate joy— he attained growth, becoming exquisitely beautiful through unsurpassed purity; and he was honored by heaps of divine, wondrous flowers of unrestrained fragrance, which fulfill all desired aims.
May that mass of wish-fulfilling creepers in the form of the matted locks of the Lotus-Bearer stand for the attainment of your prosperity.
Those upon whom the Lord Amitābha, having cast off his other dwelling, bestows liberation from bondage and produces an extraordinary adornment with his own body;
those who destroy all worldly fragrance and anoint every direction with incomparable, intense perfume.
May those extremely formidable matted locks of Laṅkeśa, which inevitably lead to death, remove your misfortunes. || 95 ||
Her matted locks are not a mass of snares for binding the minds of all people;
nor is her loveliness a flood of nectar capable of sustaining the lives of a world distressed by the fire of suffering;
nor is she a lotus that dispels the defects and afflictions caused by the whip of the horse of Death to the wicked who must be subdued.
May the Lord whose hair is embraced by the moon-like Jina grant you the fulfillment of your cherished hopes and prosperity. 96.

With his lips bitten, blazing with a malevolent gaze, and resembling the fire of cosmic destruction— fanned by the impetuous joy of devouring the three worlds as they tremble from the delusion of a universal conflagration wrought by the spreading, unrestrained expansion of his tawny radiance— he is [gazed upon] by Lakṣmī, who has fixed her aim upon him following the horse-headed Viṣṇu.
May the gaze of the World-Lord’s Consort, born in this world and momentarily distressed by incomparable compassion, protect you. 97.
Today, the world clearly moves toward destruction; all great mountains swiftly go to powder, and even the infinite oceans dry up.
Thus, from the forehead of him whose brow is terrible with the knitting of the frown of Death—
May he be victorious, who, seeing the Goddess departing, was terrified by the incomparable strength of her arms. 98.
May she who is praised with hymns by those worthy of praise, who is herself the Guru of even the Gurus in this world, and who is worshipped by those worthy of worship;
she whose manifest power for protecting the entire universe has been acquired through many kalpas without artifice;
and who, like the lotus-born Brahmā, has emerged as incomparable compassion itself to sever the suffering of the world—may she be present.
May Tārā, who removes the heavy and shimmering causes [of suffering] from within the prison-womb of saṃsāra, protect you. || 99 ||
His virtues are sung by the assembly of gods; he is to be grasped by those who stand at the forefront of Bṛhaspati;

he is profound with the clear movements of the non-submerged constellations; he is accessible to those moving like swans with fierce strides; his greatness is proclaimed by those singing deeply; and he possesses but a small portion of the multitude of things to be sung.
May the entire multitude of virtues of the Victorious One, who is rightly to be attained, protect you—those virtues which are the lotus-born from the speech of the Sugata. || 100 ||

May I too, as a poet, be a devotee at the feet of Avalokiteśvara in birth after birth; may my intellect be naturally inclined toward seeking refuge, and may I perform the great task of benefiting others. (101)
The *Śrīlokeśvaraśataka*, composed by the great minister Śrīvajradatta, is completed.
